name: Close

field_reviews.reason: developer.close.com/api/overview/oauth-authentication documents a full OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow (app.close.com/oauth2/authorize -> api.close.com/oauth2/token with grant_type=authorization_code, refresh tokens via offline_access). Docs recommend OAuth for user-facing integrations, which is the relevant primary for a multi-tenant integration; API keys are the alternative for internal/server-side use.

developer.close.com/api/overview lists exactly two methods: API keys (HTTP Basic with key as username, empty password) and OAuth 2.0. The Basic mechanism carries an api_key credential, matching the draft's own note.

close.com/pricing confirms 'Start your free 14-day trial—no credit card required' and four paid tiers from $9-19/user/month (annual/monthly) with no permanent free plan; help.close.com confirms API keys and OAuth apps are created self-serve under Settings -> Developer.

API overview documents full CRUD over leads, contacts, opportunities, activities (calls, emails, SMS, notes, meetings), custom fields, webhooks and an event log, plus an OpenAPI spec at api.close.com/api/openapi.json.
Base URL https://api.close.com/api/v1 with standard REST conventions and JSON; official remote MCP endpoint at https://mcp.close.com/mcp (HTTP Streamable, no SSE).

developer.close.com/mcp documents the vendor-hosted server at mcp.close.com/mcp with OAuth 2.0 DCR or Close-API-Key/Close-Scope header auth and the three scopes named in the draft (mcp.read, mcp.write_safe, mcp.write_destructive). docs.composio.dev/toolkits/close confirms the CLOSE toolkit (API_KEY auth, 6 tools, 0 triggers, category crm) exactly as drafted.
Self-serve trial signup, self-serve API keys and OAuth app creation, broad documented REST API with webhooks, and an official MCP server: nothing gates immediate building.
No approval process, partner gate or paid-only API found; trial includes API access and requires no credit card.

notes: Independently fetched developer.close.com/api/overview, the OAuth authentication page, developer.close.com/mcp, close.com/pricing and docs.composio.dev/toolkits/close. All eight fields match the live docs, including the MCP scope names and the Composio toolkit's exact tool count. Only nuance: docs order API keys first and recommend them for scripts, so primary_auth=oauth2 is a judgment call for user-facing integrations, but both methods are fully documented and self-serve.
